findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification
findings.body: Password verification above this branch is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence and never validates that TOTP. A request containing an email, a valid backupCode, and any arbitrary nonempty totpCode therefore authenticates without the account password. This turns a backup code into a standalone login credential instead of a replacement second factor. Ensure the required primary authentication is verified regardless of which second-factor field is supplied.

findings.title: Consume backup codes atomically to prevent replay and lost updates
findings.body: Backup codes are read with the initial user lookup, checked in memory, and then overwritten using an update constrained only by user ID. Two concurrent requests can both read and successfully consume the same code, violating its single-use guarantee. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes and restore a consumed code. Use an atomic conditional update or appropriately locked transaction, and only authenticate if consumption succeeds.

findings.title: Expose backup-code recovery for external-provider 2FA logins
findings.body: When totpEmail is supplied after Google/SAML authentication, the page renders ExternalTotpFooter instead of TwoFactorFooter, so there is no 'Lost access' action and the backup-code input cannot be reached. This affects users who generated backup codes as CAL accounts and subsequently linked an external provider—the account-linking flow preserves their enabled 2FA and codes. Such users cannot use their saved recovery codes after losing their authenticator. Supporting this flow also requires adjusting the credentials provider's external-provider guard, which currently rejects requests without totpCode even when backupCode is supplied.
